judged_text: The design establishes two concurrent writers for the same credential records — a push webhook (app-credential.ts) and a pull refresh endpoint (refreshOAuthTokens) — with no coordination, versioning, or single-source-of-truth rule for which copy wins. When parent and child both refresh (e.g. a scheduled refresh on cal.com racing a booking-triggered refresh on the child), each side persists its own newer token and last-writer-wins; for providers that rotate refresh tokens the losing side's stored refresh_token is invalidated, permanently breaking that user's integration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new webhook writer that upserts `prisma.credential` records (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` does `credential.update/create` with `data: { key: keys }`) and also introduces new refresh flows that update the same credential records during token refresh (e.g. `GoogleCalendarService`, `Office365CalendarService`, `Zoom` adapters call `prisma.credential.update` with refreshed token material). There is no diff-visible coordination mechanism (no optimistic locking/version field, no "source of truth" guard, no conflict resolution), so concurrent updates can be last-writer-wins and clobber each other. The specific "parent vs child" race and "rotating refresh tokens permanently breaking" outcome depends on external deployment behavior not shown here, but the uncoordinated concurrent-writer design concern is grounded in the new code paths.
